https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Mario David Coronado Juarez Photograph: Hispanic Center of Western Michigan via Instagram View image in fullscreen Mario David Coronado Juarez Photograph: Hispanic Center of Western Michigan via Instagram ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) Democrats demand answers after man dies in car crash during ICE traffic stop in Michigan Mario David Coronado Juarez was killed when his car struck a tree and burst into flames as he attempted to avoid ICE Richard Luscombe Thu 24 Sep 2026 09.36 EDT Last modified on Thu 24 Sep 2026 12.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Leading Democrats and immigration advocates in Michigan are demanding transparency from federal authorities after a man died in a fiery car crash as he attempted to avoid agents from Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ). Mario David Coronado Juarez, a Guatemalan national, was killed Sunday in Grand Rapids when his vehicle struck a tree at high speed and burst into flames shortly after the ICE officers tried to conduct a traffic stop. His death came the same day as two other incidents of ICE violence, as critics say officers are pursuing increasingly aggressive tactics in support of Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown. In Austin, Texas, an agent shot and wounded a Venezuelan man, Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, who was working as a Door Dash delivery driver. And in Evanston, Illinois, a US citizen needed hospital treatment for injuries sustained when two ICE agents attempted to arrest him in an apparent case of mistaken identity . A Washington Post analysis in July found that at least 17 motorists had been shot by federal immigration agents during enforcement operations, and six of those died. Gretchen Whitmer, the Democratic Michigan governor, said she had ordered a review of the Grand Rapids incident. Joseph Trigg, chief of the Grand Rapids police department, asked the Michigan state police (MSP) to join the investigation, noting in a statement that his own traffic detectives had been “limited in their ability” to obtain information from federal agencies. “MSP, under the direction of the governor and attorney general, may be in a better position to determine the timeframe and any other potentially relevant circumstances, and any next steps that may be appropriate,” Trigg’s statement said. According to the immigration advocacy group Movimiento Cosecha in Grand Rapids, Coronado, 36, was from the Guatemalan city of San Marcos, and came to the US alone to work as a construction worker and send money home for his wife and three young children. Hillary Scholten, a Democratic Michigan congresswoman, said she had asked ICE for an explanation of its agents’ actions prior to the accident. “No traffic stop should end with a fatality. Something went wrong, and we need to know what and how,” she said in a statement that requested “a transparent investigation into facts we don’t yet know.” ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), its parent agency , have not yet commented on the incident. https://telex.hu/english/2026/11/09/hung.text: At the request of the Hungarian Helsinki Committee, the ombudsman has initiated proceedings against Hungary’s OTP Bank, as the human rights organization alleges that the bank arbitrarily closed the bank accounts of individuals who have been officially recognized by Hungarian authorities as refugees, subjecting them thereby to discriminatory treatment. The Hungarian Helsinki Committee cited the case of a Russian psychologist, who was forced to leave Russia and has been living in Hungary since 2019. The individual was officially granted refugee status last year, but OTP unilaterally closed their bank account, which had at that point been active for six years. According to the organization, the Russian citizen attempted to update their records with the bank during a data verification process conducted to prevent money laundering, but the institution refused to accept their documents confirming their refugee status-including the official certificate issued by the Hungarian immigration authorities. OTP simply informed the individual that they must either voluntarily close their bank account or the bank would close it, which would result in them losing access to their money. They ultimately transferred their savings to an account they had previously opened at another bank. According to the organization, many refugees living in Hungary have experienced a similar situation recently, including some whose funds were frozen by the bank and whose debit cards were deactivated. In order to use its services, OTP requires refugees to present a residence permit, but according to Helsinki, the condition is impossible to meet, and there is no Hungarian law stipulating it. The CSO has submitted a public interest claim to the Commissioner for Fundamental Rights, who has initiated proceedings against the financial institution.
